title: introduce-tenant-data-sovereignty-hook-and-key-policy-guardrails
author: Maya Patel
release_notes: Add tenant-level data sovereignty enforcement hook and key policy guardrails; opt-in rollout behind feature flag; no breaking API changes.
commits: add: tenancy sovereignty hook and enforcement module
chore: add unit tests and mocks for region check
feat: integrate key-policy guardrail into kms-allocator
fix: loosen default behavior for legacy-tenants behind feature flag
docs: update security-runbook and operator notes
body: Summary: Add a tenant-level data sovereignty enforcement hook and a KMS key-policy guardrails layer that together make it possible to declare per-tenant region pinning and ensure keys used for tenant crypto are region-anchored or subject to approved cross-region fallback. Motivation: Customers in regulated industries require deterministic enforcement of data residency and key locality. Existing controls were split between the auth layer and KMS allocator but lacked an enforceable inbound hook during request acceptance and a systematic guardrail for key allocation that prevents accidental cross-region key usage. This PR implements an enforcement hook in the authorization service and a guardrail in the KMS allocator so that: - New tenant metadata with data_residency scope is checked at creation and enforced on write/read operations (opt-in via feature flag). - KMS allocator validates requested key locations against tenant residency; if a mismatch occurs the allocator will either reject the request or return a scoped, auditable fallback token depending on policy. - Audit events include an immutable residency assertion (residency_claim:region=eu-west-1) so downstream audit-forwarders and SRE tooling can correlate region decisions. What I changed (high level): - services/authorization: added sovereignty_hook.rs which exposes a RequestSovereigntyChecker trait and a default implementation that consults tenant metadata and feature flags. Hook runs early in auth pipeline before route execution. - services/kms: added guardrail checks into kms_allocator.go to validate candidate CMK providers against tenant residency, with a configurable policy enum (enforce|allow-with-proof|warn-only). - integrations/audit: added residency_claim propagation to forwarder_adapter.rb so audit packets carry the claim and KMS provider metadata. - docs: operator-focused rollout notes and guardrails.md describing policy matrices and how to map tenant claims to provider allowlists. - tests: unit tests and integration mocks for the authority + allocator interaction; added tests that simulate a cross-region key allocation attempt. Backwards compatibility and rollout: - Default behavior for tenants without a residency claim is unchanged. - New behavior is controlled by feature flag security.tenant_residency_enforcement. - For existing tenants that opt in, a migration check validates that their default CMKs are in-scope; we provide an operator script (docs/operators/sovereignty-rollout.md) to assist rekeying. Security considerations: - Added an explicit deny path in the auth hook to fail-fast on mismatched residency claims—this prevents accidental data export to disallowed regions. - Guardrails include an allow-with-proof mode to support approved cross-regioning workflows. Audit and observability: - Emits audit events with keys: residency_claim, kms_provider, kms_key_id, policy_decision and correlates to request_id so SRE can add alerting rules. - Console dashboards will surface 'residency-violations' metric (new meter name: security.residency.violation). Testing and CI notes: - Unit tests included for both allow and deny paths. - Integration test uses a small mock KMS provider host to verify allocator behavior under network error and fallback conditions. - CI initially failed lint on an infra import; fixed by renaming a helper and rerunning — final CI status: pass. Review thread (high level): - Ravi Singh (reviewer): requested explicit opt-in for tenant-level enforcement; asked for clearer operator migration steps. Response: moved rollout notes into docs/operators and added a pre-check script; feature flag defaulted to off. - Clara Novak: asked for an additional audit field to record the original requested-region vs chosen-region. Response: added kms_provider and original_region keys to the audit packet. - Jordan Lee: requested more unit coverage around the allow-with-proof flow. Response: added tests and a small integration scenario that exercises proof tokens. Merge outcome: PR approved by all reviewers and merged by squash on 2025-11-20 after CI green. Linear/Jira: references ENG-9921 for product spec, SEC-314 for threat-model signoff, and SUP-4578 for a customer support escalation that motivated the initial design. Operational runbook: operator-facing doc includes steps for dry-run mode, metrics to watch (security.residency.violation, kms.guardrail.denied), and recommended cron job to find tenants with out-of-scope CMKs. Checklist: - [x] Design doc reviewed (ENG-9921) - [x] Threat model / security review (SEC-314) - [x] Unit + integration tests added - [x] Docs for operators and ops playbook - [x] Feature-flagged and non-breaking by default Notes: This PR intentionally leaves UI and Console policy management for a follow-up so the rollout can be validated in environments where operators prefer CLI/manual migration. Follow-ups: - Console: admin UI for region policy mapping (follow-up ticket ENG-10045) - Metric alerts: add default alert recipe to SLO toolkit (follow-up ticket ENG-10046)
